stem: When we look at a map, from which viewpoint is the surface of the area shown?
options: As if viewed from directly above it
As if viewed from the side at ground level
As if viewed from deep below the ground
As if viewed at a slant from a hilltop
explanation: Correct option: (A). A map shows the surface as if you are viewing it from the top. A side view, a view from below or a slanting view from a hilltop is not how a map represents an area.

stem: A student says, "A map can only show a small area like a village, because a big area cannot fit on paper." Which response is correct?
options: Wrong; with a scale, a map can show a village or the whole world.
Right; big areas such as countries can be shown only on a globe.
Right; big areas fit on paper only if their directions are left out.
Wrong; big areas fit because maps show every building as it is.
explanation: Correct option: (A). A map can represent a small area, a district or state, or even the whole world, because a scale lets a large area fit on a small sheet. Countries are shown on maps all the time, directions are still shown, and maps use symbols rather than drawing every building.

stem: A city map has the scale 1 cm = 500 m. What does this mean?

Each 500 cm on the map stands for 1 m on the ground

stem: A rectangular playground, 40 m long and 30 m wide, is drawn using the scale 1 cm = 10 m. The diagonal on the drawing measures 5 cm. What is the real length of the diagonal?
options: 70 m, by adding the length and the width
5 m, as each centimetre stands for 1 m
500 m, as each centimetre stands for 100 m
50 m, as each centimetre stands for 10 m
explanation: Correct option: (D). Real distance = map distance x scale = 5 cm x 10 m per cm = 50 m. Adding length and width (70 m) is not how a diagonal is found, and the scale here is 10 m per cm, not 1 m or 100 m per cm.

stem: On a map of India, a ruler 2.5 cm long stands for 500 km. Two places are 5 cm apart on this map. What is the real distance between them?
options: 250 km
500 km
explanation: Correct option: (C). 5 cm is 5 / 2.5 = 2 times the ruler length, so the real distance is 2 x 500 km = 1,000 km. 250 km halves instead of doubling, 500 km ignores the extra length, and 1,250 km wrongly multiplies 2.5 by 500.

stem: Map P of a district uses the scale 1 cm = 1 km, and Map Q of the same district uses 1 cm = 10 km. Which statement is correct?
options: Map P shows the district larger, so it can show more detail.
Map Q shows the district larger, so it can show more detail.
Both maps show the district at exactly the same size.
Map Q must be wrong, since a district has only one scale.
explanation: Correct option: (A). On Map P, 10 km of ground takes 10 cm, while on Map Q it takes only 1 cm, so Map P draws the district ten times longer and has room for more detail. The two maps are not the same size, and the same area can be drawn at many different scales.

stem: Evaluate the statement: "All parallels of latitude have the same length."
options: True, because every parallel is a full circle around the Earth
False, because parallels are half-circles from pole to pole
False, because parallels get shorter from the Equator to the poles
True, because every parallel runs parallel to the Equator
explanation: Correct option: (C). Each parallel is a circle, but the circles grow smaller from the Equator (the largest) towards the poles, so their lengths differ. Being full circles or being parallel to the Equator does not make them equal, and half-circles from pole to pole are meridians, not parallels.

stem: Read the case. Why is it still full daylight in Porbandar when the sun has already set in Tinsukia?

stem: Why do most countries adopt one standard time instead of letting each place use its own local time?
